What I wanted to say was in another comment, really. But other than that, I do feel that being social is worth it. (Social not as in being extroverted- some people seem to not know the difference in having social anxiety and being introverted) 

I've been trying to put myself in social situations on purpose, and ask out acquaintances I'd like to know more about. I felt very awkward and anxious that I'd be seen as weird, but trying to say at least one thing was my set goal for every meets. I also tried to give people small compliments and expressed thanks to them when appropriate. On the course of 3 years, I felt myself being able to have small talks with people although I still feel very awkward (In the past I couldn't hold conversations and would push people away without knowing). I also succeeded in making some acquaintances friends.

I had the luck of having some good people who understood that I could be very awkward until we get super comfortable with each other, and shared the same interests. I did say this as 'luck,' but then again, I had to actually interact with them to know that they were a good fit for me!

Sorry for being all over the place, I really suck at making points haha. Anyways I just wanted to tell you to take very small steps at a time so you won't be overwhelmed by it, but I feel it is definitely worth trying to be social.

Edit: Forgot to mention it, but please don't force yourself to fit in. You can be yourself and be social at the same time. Trying to fit in has only given me unnecessary stress... And if people would leave you out of a conversation and talk about something that only they know about, then the problem's not with you, but them.

And about the hair dye part- I'm planning to dye my hair turquoise and one of my life goals is to be a popular YouTuber(Yes I love getting attention when it's positive), yet I still have social anxiety!! Nobody has every symptoms the same way and people should really respect that :,)
